subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or should default steer remain boundary-based?
rationale: The remaining request is not a narrow bug fix: it changes shared runtime semantics, channel UX, session-state handling, and the relationship between existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate queue mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current model-boundary steering as the supported default and limit related fixes to ensuring messages reach that existing policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Make default steer use the stronger lifecycle only after explicit upgrade proof across channels and runtimes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate queue mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate from the active non-streaming steering replacement and related reply-run lifecycle work.
